spots.name: Gyeongbokgung
spots.summary: Gyeongbokgung is a former royal palace in Seoul, South Korea. Established in 1395, it was the first royal palace of the Joseon dynasty, and is now one of the most significant tourist attractions in the country.

spots.name: National Museum of Korea
spots.summary: The National Museum of Korea (Korean: 국립중앙박물관) is the flagship museum of Korean history and art in South Korea.

spots.name: Cheonggyecheon
spots.summary: Cheonggyecheon is a 10.9-kilometre-long (6.8 mi) stream and public space in downtown Seoul, South Korea.

photo.author: kallerna This photo was taken with Fujifilm X-T30

spots.name: Changdeokgung

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Changdeokgung is a former royal palace in Seoul, South Korea. A UNESCO World Heritage Site and a Historic Site of South Korea, it is among the best preserved of all Korean palaces. It and its neighboring palace Changgyeonggung have together been called the "East Palace".

spots.name: Cheong Wa Dae

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Cheong Wa Dae (Korean: 청와대), also known as the Blue House, is the executive office and residence of the president of South Korea.

spots.name: Namsan Seoul Tower
spots.summary: Namsan Seoul Tower, also known as the YTN Seoul Tower, Namsan Tower, Seoul Tower or N Seoul Tower, is a communication and observation tower located on the summit of Namsan in central Seoul, South Korea.

spots.name: Deoksugung

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Deoksugung, also called Deoksu Palace or Deoksugung Palace, is a former royal palace in Seoul, South Korea. It was the main palace during the Korean Empire (1897–1910) and is now a major tourist attraction. It has a mix of traditional Korean and Western architecture that reflects its history.

spots.name: Gilt-bronze Maitreya in Meditation
spots.summary: The Gilt-bronze Maitreya in Meditation is a gilt-bronze statue of Maitreya seated in meditation and is one of the best known and most highly regarded Korean Buddhist sculptures. Now part of the collection of the National Museum of Korea, it was designated as the 78th national treasure of Korea.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Gilt-bronze Maitreya in Meditation (National Treasure No. 78)

spots.name: Gold Crown from Cheonmachong
spots.summary: The Gold Crown from Cheonmachong is a crown from the Silla dynasty. It was discovered in Cheonmachong tomb in Gyeongju, North Gyeongsang Province, South Korea, in 1973. Considered the largest and most exquisite surviving ancient Korean crown, it was designated a National Treasure of South Korea in 1978.

spots.name: Gwanghwamun
spots.summary: Gwanghwamun is the main and south gate of the palace Gyeongbokgung, in Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea. It is located at a three-way intersection at the northern end of Sejongno.

spots.name: Jongmyo
spots.summary: Jongmyo (Korean: 종묘) is a Confucian royal ancestral shrine in the Jongno District of Seoul, South Korea. It was originally built during the Joseon period (1392–1897) for memorial services for deceased kings and queens.

spots.name: Gwanghwamun Square
spots.summary: Gwanghwamun Square (Korean: 광화문광장), a.k.a. Gwanghwamun Plaza, is a public square located in Sejongno, Jongno-gu, Seoul, in front of Gyeongbokgung.

spots.name: Myeongdong Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral Church of Our Lady of the Immaculate Conception, informally known as Myeongdong Cathedral (명동대성당), is the national cathedral of the Archdiocese of Seoul. Located in the Myeongdong neighbourhood of Jung District, Seoul, South Korea, it is the seat of the Archbishop of Seoul, Peter Chung Soon-taick.

names.es: Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepción de la Virgen María

spots.name: Namdaemun
spots.summary: Namdaemun, a.k.a. the Sungnyemun, is the southern gate of The Eight Gates of Seoul making part of the Seoul City Wall marking the city's original boundary during the Joseon period, although the city has since significantly outgrown it after that.

spots.name: War Memorial of Korea

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The War Memorial of Korea (Korean: 전쟁기념관) is a museum located in Yongsan-dong, Yongsan-gu, Seoul, South Korea. It opened in 1994 on the former site of the army headquarters to exhibit and memorialize the military history of Korea.

names.it: Monumento ai Caduti della Corea del Sud

spots.name: Bukhansan Monument
spots.summary: Bukhansan Monument is a stone monument dated roughly to the 6th century CE. It was designated as the 3rd National Treasure of Korea on December 20, 1962.

names.ja: 北漢山新羅真興王巡狩碑
names.zh: 北漢山新羅真興王巡狩碑

spots.name: Samsung Town
spots.summary: The Samsung Town is a major office park in Seocho-gu in Seoul, South Korea. It serves as the IT and electronics hub for the multinational corporation Samsung.

spots.name: Gyeongcheonsa Pagoda

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Gyeongcheonsa Pagoda is National Treasure of Korea No. 86. It was designated by the South Korean government on December 20, 1962.

spots.name: Yoido Full Gospel Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Yoido Full Gospel Church is a Pentecostal church affiliated with the Assemblies of God on Yeouido in Seoul, South Korea. With about 870,000 members, it is the largest Pentecostal Christian congregation in South Korea. Founded by David Yonggi Cho and Choi Ja-shil in 1958, the church is presently led by Young Hoon Lee.

names.es: Iglesia del Evangelio Pleno de Yoido

spots.name: Changgyeonggung
spots.summary: Changgyeonggung is a palace located in Seoul, South Korea.

spots.name: Seoul City Wall

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Seoul City Wall or Hanyang Doseong (한양도성) is a defensive wall first built by the King Taejo of Joseon dynasty to defend the downtown area of Joseon's capital city Hanseong. It was designated as a Historic Site of South Korea in 1963, and is currently a tourist attraction around Downtown Seoul.

spots.name: Statue of King Sejong
spots.summary: Statue of King Sejong is located at the Sejongno, Gwanghwamun Plaza in Downtown Seoul, South Korea. It is dedicated to the 15th century Korean monarch, Sejong the Great, the fourth king of Joseon dynasty and one of Korea's most famous historical figures. The statue is considered one of Seoul's major landmarks.

spots.name: Seoul City Hall
spots.summary: Seoul City Hall is a governmental building for the Seoul Metropolitan Government in South Korea, in charge of the administrative affairs of Seoul. It is located in Taepyeongno, Jung District, at the heart of Seoul.

spots.name: Seoul Metropolitan Council
spots.summary: The Seoul Metropolitan Council (Korean: 서울특별시의회) is the local council of Seoul.

photo.author: Wei-Te Wong from Taipei City, Taiwan, Republic of China

spots.name: Statue of Peace
spots.summary: The Statue of Peace, often shortened to Sonyeosang in Korean or Shōjo-zō in Japanese and sometimes called the Comfort Woman Statue , is a symbol of the women forced into sexual slavery—known euphemistically as comfort women—by the Imperial Japanese Armed Forces before and during World War II—specifically, the period from the beginning of the Second Sino-Japanese War until the end of the Pacific Wa

spots.name: Parc1

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Parc1 (Korean: 파크원) is a complex of buildings in Yeouido, Seoul, South Korea. It stands 333 m (1,093 ft) tall and contains 69 floors. Construction stopped in 2011 but resumed in early 2017.

spots.name: Statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin
spots.summary: The statue of Admiral Yi Sun-sin is located at the street Sejongno, Gwanghwamun Plaza, Seoul, South Korea. It is dedicated to the 16th-century Korean war hero, admiral Yi Sun-sin. It is considered one of Seoul's major landmarks and has been called "one of the most important instances of Korean public art".

spots.name: Geunjeongjeon

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Geunjeongjeon is the main hall of the palace Gyeongbokgung in Seoul, South Korea. It was used for major events like ceremonies and the issuing of edicts. It is a designated National Treasure of South Korea.

spots.name: Seoul Plaza
spots.summary: Seoul Plaza (Korean: 서울광장) is a central plaza located in front of Seoul City Hall at Taepyeongno, Jung District, Seoul, South Korea. It was reopened on 1 May 2004, by Seoul Metropolitan Government, with the purpose of providing the public an open space.

spots.name: Seodaemun Prison

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Seodaemun Prison History Hall (Korean: 서대문형무소역사관) is a museum and former prison in Seodaemun District, Seoul, South Korea. Imperial Japan, then the overlord of Korea, began its construction in 1907.

spots.name: National Folk Museum of Korea

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: National Folk Museum of Korea (Korean: 국립민속박물관) is a national museum located on the grounds of Gyeongbokgung in Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea. It uses replicas of historical objects to illustrate the history of traditional life of the Korean people.

spots.name: Bongeunsa

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Bongeunsa is a Korean Buddhist temple located in Samseong-dong, Gangnam District, Seoul, South Korea. It was founded in 794 during the reign of King Wonseong by State Preceptor Yeonhoe, then the highest ranking monk of Silla. The temple was originally named Gyeonseongsa.

spots.name: Jogyesa

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Jogyesa is the chief temple of the Jogye Order of Korean Buddhism. The building dates back to the late 14th century and became the order's chief temple in 1936. It thus plays a leading role in the current state of Seon Buddhism in South Korea.

spots.name: Crown of Baekje
spots.summary: The gold diadem ornaments of King Muryeong is a pair of golden ornaments made in the kingdom of Baekje, Three Kingdoms of Korea which were excavated in 1971 in the tomb of King Muryeong in Gongju city, South Chungcheong Province, South Korea.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Gold Diadem Ornaments of King Muryeong

spots.name: Dongdaemun
spots.summary: Heunginjimun, a.k.a. Dongdaemun, is one of The Eight Gates of Seoul in the Seoul City Wall, a prominent landmark in central Seoul, South Korea. The Korean name "Dongdaemun" means "Great East Gate," and it was so named because it was the major eastern gate in the wall that surrounded Seoul during the Joseon period.

spots.name: Art Center Nabi

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Art Center Nabi (Korean: 아트센터나비) is an art museum in Seorin-dong, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea. It was relocated to the 4th floor of SK building of SK Group in 2000 and reborn as digital art museum.

names.ja: アート・センター・ナビ

spots.name: Inwangsan
spots.summary: Inwangsan (Korean: 인왕산) is a mountain in central Seoul, South Korea. It is in parts of Jongno District and Seodaemun District and has a height of 338 m (1,109 ft). The name literally means "compassionate/benevolent king" in Korean.

spots.name: Gyeonghoeru
spots.summary: Gyeonghoeru is an elevated banquet hall in the palace Gyeongbokgung in Seoul, South Korea. It is a designated National Treasure.

spots.name: International Finance Center Seoul
spots.summary: International Finance Center Seoul (Korean: 서울국제금융센터), commonly known as IFC Seoul, is a mixed-use integrated commercial development in Yeouido-dong, Yeongdeungpo District, Seoul, South Korea. The IFC project is one of the first large-scale developments in Korea, led by an international consortium.

names.ja: ソウル国際金融センター

spots.name: Ilmin Museum of Art

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Ilmin Museum of Art is a private art museum of South Korea, located on Sejongno street in Jongno District, a central district of Seoul, known for exhibiting mainly Korean art.

spots.name: Jongno Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Jongno Tower is a 33-story office building in Jongno, Seoul. Its top floor used to have a restaurant and bar, both of which closed in 2022. It is famous for its view of Jongno and other areas of Seoul. The tower is located near Jonggak Station of Seoul Subway Line 1. The 23rd to 30th floors are hollow.

names.ja: 鍾路タワー（ミレニアムタワー）

spots.name: Chōsen Shrine

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Chōsen Shrine was the most important Shinto shrine during the Japanese colonial period in Korea. It was built in 1925 in Seoul and destroyed soon after the end of colonial rule in 1945.

spots.name: Wongaksa Pagoda

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Wongaksa Pagoda is a 12-meter tall, ten story marble pagoda located in Tapgol Park, Seoul, South Korea. The pagoda is considered by art historians to be one of the finest Korean pagodas., designated as a National Treasure of South Korea in 1962.

spots.name: Youngnak Presbyterian Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Youngnak Presbyterian Church (Korean: 영락교회) is a church in Seoul, South Korea. It was founded on 2 December 1945 by Kyung-Chik Han, who later won the 1992 Templeton Prize.

spots.name: National Palace Museum of Korea
spots.summary: The National Palace Museum of Korea (Korean: 국립고궁박물관) is a national museum located in Gyeongbokgung, Seoul, South Korea.

spots.name: COEX Aquarium
spots.summary: The SEA LIFE COEX, Seoul Aquarium is an aquarium located within the Starfield COEX Mall in the Gangnam District of Seoul, South Korea. The aquarium opened in 2000.

spots.name: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art

hours.note: Closed Tue, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: The National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Korea is a contemporary art museum with four branches in Gwacheon, Deoksugung, Seoul and Cheongju. The museum was established in 1969 as the country's only national art museum dedicated to Korean modern and contemporary art, while also presenting international art.
spots.wikipediaTitle: National Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art

names.es: Museo Nacional de Arte Moderno y Contemporáneo

spots.name: Seongsu Bridge
spots.summary: The Seongsu Bridge (Korean: 성수대교), sometimes spelled Sŏngsu Bridge, is a cantilever bridge over the Han River, connecting the Seongdong and Gangnam districts of Seoul, South Korea.

photo.author: Kaitak89(talk / Contributions) at the Korean Wikipedia

spots.name: Tapgol Park
spots.summary: Tapgol Park, formerly Pagoda Park, is a public park located at 99 Jongno, Jongno District, Seoul, South Korea. It is 1.50561 ha in area. The park was previously known as Pagoda Park until May 28, 1992.

spots.name: Sejong Center
spots.summary: Sejong Center for the Performing Arts (Korean: 세종문화회관) is the largest arts and cultural complex in Seoul, South Korea. It has an interior area of 53,202m². It is situated in the center of the capital, on Sejongno, a main road that cuts through the capital city of the Joseon Dynasty.

spots.name: Seoul Metropolitan Library

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Seoul Metropolitan Library is a Metropolitan Library on Taepyeongno, Jung District, Seoul, South Korea. It faces the Seoul City Hall and Seoul Plaza, and is next to the City Hall Station on Seoul Subway Line 1.

spots.name: Seoul Anglican Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Cathedral Church of St Mary the Virgin and St Nicholas, or the Seoul Anglican Cathedral, is an Anglican cathedral in Downtown Seoul, South Korea. It is the mother church of both the Anglican Church of Korea and the Diocese of Seoul.

names.es: Catedral de Santa María la Virgen y San Nicolás

spots.name: Unhyeongung

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Unhyeongung, also known as Unhyeongung Royal Residence, is a former Korean royal residence located at 114-10 Unni-dong, Jongno-gu, Seoul. It was formerly the residence of the Heungseon Daewongun, who served as a prince regent of Joseon Korea in the 19th century and fathered Emperor Gojong.

spots.name: Bumingwan
spots.summary: Bumingwan is a historic building in Seoul, South Korea. It previously served as the building for Korea's National Assembly. It now currently serves as a building for the Seoul Metropolitan Council. It was designated a Registered Cultural Heritage in 2002.

spots.name: HiKR Ground

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: HiKR Ground is a tourist information and cultural center in Seoul, South Korea.

spots.name: Dongmyo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Dongmyo is a myo shrine in Downtown Seoul, South Korea. It was one of Guandi Temple built in honour of the 3rd century Chinese military commander, Guan Yu.

spots.name: Seoullo 7017
spots.summary: Seoullo 7017, also known as the Seoul Skygarden or Skypark, is an elevated linear park in Seoul, built atop a former highway overpass. The path, which is about 1 kilometre (0.62 mi) in length and lined with 24,000 plants, is similar to New York City's High Line.

spots.name: 31 Building

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: 31 Building (Korean: 31빌딩), also called Samil Building, is an office building in Seoul, South Korea. Completed in 1970, the 31 Building was the tallest building in Seoul until 1979, when Lotte Hotel Seoul was completed.

spots.name: Hwangudan
spots.summary: Hwangudan was a shrine complex that still partially stands in Jung District, Seoul, South Korea. The complex consisted of two main buildings: a coronation site and Hwanggungu. The coronation site was built in late 1897 and destroyed in 1913. Hwanggungu was built in 1899 and still stands today.

spots.name: Dongdaemun History & Culture Park
spots.summary: Dongdaemun History & Culture Park (Korean: 동대문역사문화공원) is a park in Jung District, Seoul, South Korea. It is on the location of the former Dongdaemun Stadium.

spots.name: Shinsegae Department Store Gangnam Branch
spots.summary: It is a popular shopping spot in Seoul that often hosts famous pop-up stores, always offering new experiences. It is a great place for gourmets as there are many delicious desserts and various restaurants. spots.name: Rice Museum
spots.summary: It is a space where you can learn about the history of rice.

spots.name: T.um
spots.summary: The future of technology can often be seen today in South Korea, and SK Telecom have created a museum dedicated to it! Exhibits change frequently due to the rapid pace of technology being shown. Preschoolers not allowed. Online pre-registration necessary, make sure to reserve early as its gets full weeks in advance.

spots.name: The Hyundai Seoul
spots.summary: A Hyundai Department Store brand, it's home to all things fashion, hip-hop, food, and dessert.

spots.summary: This state-of-the-art complex combines a massive underground mall, luxury hotels, office towers, convention center, and international trade center. Parts of the mall have aged considerably since its debut, but it still features mid-to-upscale shopping, entertainment, and Korean and Western food options. spots.name: SeMA Bunker
spots.summary: A rather mysterious former bunker built during the 1970s military government. It was discovered in 2005 during the bus transfer center construction, and was opened as a gallery in 2017. It is part of the Seoul Museum of Arts.

Bukchon Observatory

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Provides a sweeping view of Bukchon Village and the greater Seoul cityscape, with Lotte Tower and the palace both clearly visible. It’s humble: clearly a converted apartment, and so tucked away its easy to miss, but it’s a great place to rest and take in the views, with beverage (tea, coffee) included as part of admission.

spots.name: Bukchon Oriental Culture Museum

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: You can see various exhibitions of the museum, and there is an observatory where you can see Seoul City Wall and Gyeongbokgung Palace.

spots.name: Apple House Isu
spots.summary: It is a snack bar that is famous for its instant tteokbokki and pan-fried mandu in sauce. The store is spacious and clean, and its efficient operation is achieved by introducing a self-service system. spots.name: Cafe Gongmyeong Yeonnam Branch
spots.summary: It is a large cafe that offers top-class coffee and fresh baked bakery with cozy interior design. This is a space where customers can enjoy a variety of desserts, with ample seats and cozy lighting to help them relax. spots.name: Café Pipe
spots.summary: An emotional cafe located near Isu Station, it offers a variety of desserts and drinks, and features a dessert lineup that changes every day. The interior of the cafe has a cozy and comfortable atmosphere, and as it is located on the first and third floors, it offers a variety of seating options. In particular, Dutch apple pies and pavlova are considered popular menus, and 'Tiffy', a signature dri

spots.name: Dangsan Red Jjukkumi
spots.summary: Known for its spicy webfoot octopus dishes, it is a restaurant that offers a wide variety of webfoot octopus menus. It is a perfect atmosphere for dinners or gatherings with friends, and the unique sauce combination using boiled eggs and tartare sauce served as a standard table setting is attractive. Fried rice is recommended as a must-have, and it can be enjoyed deliciously as it is well infused

spots.name: Flup Coffee
spots.summary: It is a space where you can concentrate in a quiet atmosphere, and it features a modern interior with a combination of midnight blue and white. There is a rooftop, so you can spend a leisurely time while enjoying the mountain view, and it provides a variety of coffee and desserts to satisfy visitors. In particular, the signature menu, custard millefeuille, is a combination of crispy pastry and sof

spots.name: Gangsanok
spots.summary: Opened in 1958, the restaurant specializes in traditional soybean dishes that serve only soybean noodles in the summer and serve soybean meal for the rest of the year. It is open for only two and a half hours a day, and needs to be careful when visiting because it can be closed early when the ingredients are exhausted. It consists of thick and savory soybean soup and chewy noodles, and is served w

spots.name: Hakrim Dabang

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Opened in 1956, this is the oldest extant coffee shop (in Korean, 다방; dabang) in Seoul. Known for its vintage charm, cozy wooden interiors, and retro vibe, Hakrim Dabang offers a nostalgic experience reminiscent of the old Seoul. spots.name: Hanwoojeong
spots.summary: Korean BBQ restaurant specializing in 1++ Korean Hanwoo beef, Korea’s highest-quality beef grade. Inspired by the elegance of a traditional hanok, Hanwoojeong provides refined Korean dining and a warm, sophisticated atmosphere. Guests can experience carefully selected cuts including sirloin, striploin, tenderloin and other premium specialties, complemented by Korean side dishes and classic accompa

spots.name: lodge 190
spots.summary: Lodge 190 is a cozy café located along the Hongjecheon Stream in Seodaemun-gu, Seoul. Known for its signature French toast made with baguette and topped with seasonal fruits, the café offers a relaxing ambiance with views of Hongjecheon. The menu includes a variety of desserts, such as matcha shaved ice and yogurt bowls. Lodge 190 is also pet-friendly, making it a popular spot for visitors who wis

spots.name: Mandongjegwa
spots.summary: Located in Yeonnam-dong, this takeaway specialty store offers a wide variety of bread. The interior of the store is compact, neat, and full of savory bread. The staff kindly provides tasting bread to help customers choose. Specifically, garlic baguette is a signature menu, featuring a rich garlic sauce and a soft texture. There is a wide variety of menus, and reservations are also available for co

spots.name: No Idea Pizza
spots.summary: Using homemade dough that has been kneaded in-store, we serve chewy and digestible pizzas. There is a wide variety of unique pizza menus, and buldak sweet potato pizza and combination pizza are especially popular. The atmosphere in the store is young and casual, making it perfect for dates or meeting friends. The self-bar offers water and pickles, and takeout and delivery services are also availab

spots.name: Noryangjin Fish Market

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The floors may be dank and wet, but this is undoubtedly the freshest seafood in Seoul, with live octopuses, spiky sea urchins, giant king crabs swimming about in water tanks, buckets and bags. Buy some fresh fish (try bargaining if you can), and head to the restaurants in the back row, where they'll prepare your food as requested. There's a wholesale auction at 02:00, where fishmongers bid for pro

spots.name: Pioni Hongik Univ. Branch
spots.summary: A cake specialty store that has been in operation since 2008, it is famous for its fresh strawberry cream cake made using 100 percent animal whipped cream and fresh strawberries. The interior of the store is cozy and clean, and it is a popular destination for many customers as it offers a variety of drinks and cakes. In particular, cakes that are carefully made with all ingredients boast reliable

spots.name: Sadang 1038
spots.summary: Located near Sadang Station, the dessert shop specializes in handmade desserts, and uses all ingredients made and used by itself. In particular, it uses French gourmet butter and 100% domestic whipped cream to enhance the quality of its flavor. It offers a wide variety of cakes and baked snacks, and is a perfect place for anniversaries and special occasions as holecakes can also be reserved and or

spots.name: Suyeon Sanbang
spots.summary: A tea house located in an old traditional wooden house which used to be the home of the writer Lee Tae-Jun. Try the jujube (red dates) tea and the pumpkin desserts while admiring the picturesque garden. There are only very few tables available, so it pays off to come early to get one of the good tables at the window. This place is quite expensive and having a tea for two with dessert will cost you

spots.name: Yeongilman
spots.summary: A Pohang-style makhoe and cold raw fish restaurant that has been in place for 25 years, they feature fresh seafood and unique recipes. In particular, makhoe is served by mixing soybean flour and red pepper paste and wrapping it in seaweed, while cold raw fish is gaining popularity for its style of mixing it with ice. In addition, soju sales per capita are limited, providing an environment where pe

spots.name: Yeonhaejang
spots.summary: It is a restaurant specializing in pork small intestine hot pot that features a clean and modern interior, and is loved by many customers even if the waiting is long. They have gopchang hot pot with a variety of side menus, and the soup of the hot pot boasts a deep and thick taste and uses fresh gopchang without any odor. In addition, it is sold as a meal kit, so you can enjoy it easily at home.

spots.name: Joaendoseun
spots.summary: It is a cafe famous for French toast and milk tea. It is decorated with a cozy and emotional interior, and customers appreciate the moist texture and unique taste of French toast. In particular, the combination of Maldon salt and maple syrup is impressive as French toast has a crispy outside and soft inside. Customers can have a special time here, enjoying conversations with their loved ones.

spots.name: Kiki Gelato
spots.summary: This is a handmade gelato specialty store that is made in-store, and sells 12 of 200 different flavors selected every day. The gelato here boasts a chewy and rich taste using Italian ingredients, and the cute character welcomes customers both outside and inside the store. It also offers menus for dogs and can be packaged, making it a dessert place that can be enjoyed in various situations.

spots.name: YonggaHwogwo Gangnam branch
spots.summary: This is a Chinese restaurant, an innovative brand where you can enjoy about 100 kinds of ingredients in your seat without having to wait in line at the self-bar. Based on one bowl per person, you can enjoy a variety of broths, from spicy Sacheon-style malatang to light white soup to deeply brewed mushroom soup. This place has a fascinating system that train robots bring when you sit down.
